summary: Highland Butte tower: 1927 plan for an 85 ft steel tower, a 1940 80 ft replacement per the register, destroyed by the 1962 Columbus Day storm.

facts.design: Steel tower with 7x7 ft cab (80 ft per the register); a platform lookout stood on the butte before it
facts.status_note: Destroyed in the Columbus Day storm, October 12, 1962; a 1963 survey note says the tower has been blown over

events.note: Lookout camp on Highland Butte listed in a February 1916 newspaper item.
State board of forestry approved plans for an 85 ft steel tower as a central dispatcher station.
January 1928 newspaper lists a steel tower on the butte, 81 ft high, cost $45,348. Conflicts with the register's dating.
Register and firelookout.com: platform lookout built atop twin spar trees.
March 1932 account describes a 90-foot steel tower.
CCC crews built a new telephone line from North Fork Station to Highland Butte.
Register and firelookout.com: 80 ft steel tower with 7x7 cab replaced the platform.
Kathleen Morrison called to take over as fire guard lookout at Highland Butte.
Safety rail installed on the tower ladder at the request of the State Industrial Accident Commission.
Destroyed in the Columbus Day storm, October 12, 1962.
1962 district report: present plans call for inactivating the lookout.
Survey note: the lookout tower has been blown over.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com date a platform to 1929 and an 80 ft steel tower to 1940. The local history has a platform already in place by April 1927 and a steel tower reported built by January 1928. The story reports both and does not pick one.
Heights in the sources: 85 ft (1927 plans), 81 ft (January 1928 report), 90 ft (1932 account), and 80 ft (register, 1940 tower). The facts use the register's 80 ft figure, converted to 24.4 m.

corrections.why: 25.9 m is 85 ft, the height in the April 1927 plans. The register gives 80 ft (24.4 m) for the 1940 tower. Other reports give 81 ft (1928) and 90 ft (1932).

notes_for_editor: No source describes the site today, so the story says so; access is left out. The brief's height_m of 25.9 is the 85 ft planned in 1927 and is corrected to 24.4 m (80 ft, register). Whether a steel tower existed before 1940 is unresolved: the register says 1929 platform then 1940 steel tower, the local history says steel by January 1928. Staffing facts are left out because the tower is gone. Two WebSearch calls used.
